project.name: Worthy Platform Constitution Milestone 1 Contract Stratification

phases.title: Naming And Contract-Class Inventory
acceptance: Road 1 constitutional classes, legal Milestone 1 births, and reserved-only later classes are frozen without teaching illegal crate names or pseudo-bands
the Road 1 workspace routing map is explicit before Cargo manifests or seed crates are born
no platform-tier entry, derived, or cert crate is smuggled into Milestone 1 through placeholder language or speculative code
phases.instructions: Implement Phase 1 exactly as the spec now defines it. Freeze the naming inventory, operational class split, and legal birth set before any Cargo or crate work widens the tree.
phases.qa_focus: No illegal name teaching, no pseudo-band like bridge, and no deferred class quietly treated as already born.

phases.title: Cargo Workspace Topology
acceptance: cad/workspaces contains five real Road 1 sub-workspaces with their own Cargo ownership
repo root remains a thin orchestrator surface rather than the owning workspace for Road 1 packages
sub-workspace commands and whole-world orchestration both resolve the same born crates through explicit manifest routing
phases.instructions: Implement Phase 2 as the real Cargo topology cut. Make each Road 1 folder a real workspace and keep the repo root orchestration-only.
phases.qa_focus: No giant root-owned workspace, no fake workspace folders, and no central member ownership at repo root.

phases.title: Seed Crate Births
acceptance: worth-schema-core and worth-pack-registry are the only born Milestone 1 crates
each born crate has the narrow skeleton promised by the spec and owns one constitutional idea from its directory shape alone
no mixed-class helper or future Query adoption logic lands inside the seed crates
phases.instructions: Implement Phase 3 by birthing only the two legal seed crates with the exact narrow skeletons the spec names. Keep them intentionally small and responsibility-shaped.
phases.qa_focus: No mixed-class modules, no helper gravity wells, and no early Query or runtime logic inside the seed crates.

phases.title: Facade And Visibility Contract
acceptance: each born seed crate exports only through a facade-shaped public surface
internal modules remain private or crate-local and cannot be deep-imported by downstream code
facade files aggregate public exports only and do not become behavior-bearing convenience layers
phases.instructions: Implement Phase 4 as the public authority-shape step. Separate crate existence from honest public consumption and make the facade contract mechanically visible.
phases.qa_focus: No behavior in facade.rs, no convenience reexports that bypass the boundary, and no public path into internal modules.

phases.title: Boundary Rule Engine
acceptance: boundary-check enforces naming, band, tier, replay, and root-ownership rules from a real machine contract
illegal Query imports, ordinary replay imports, root-owned Road 1 packages, and worth-to-worthy dependency inversions fail mechanically
the rule engine produces named diagnostics rather than prose-only architectural warnings
phases.instructions: Implement Phase 5 as the machine-enforced boundary step. Build the rule engine and its negative fixtures before any claim that Milestone 1 is protected.
phases.qa_focus: No docs-only bans, no merged agent-context responsibilities inside the rule engine, and no delayed enforcement.

phases.title: Generated Crate Context
acceptance: crate-local AGENT_CONTEXT.md files are generated for both born seed crates from the same machine-owned boundary model
freshness validation fails stale or hand-edited generated context
crate-local orientation remains structurally aligned with the enforced constitutional class and public surface
phases.instructions: Implement Phase 6 as the generated local-orientation step. Agent context must come from machine-owned substrate, not hand-maintained prose.
phases.qa_focus: No hand-written crate context, no drift between rule engine and generated context, and no optional freshness proof.

phases.title: Exemplar Routing And Deferred Public Proof
acceptance: the foundational identity, naming, and tolerance specimen plus the pack-seam descriptor specimen are publicly routable from docs and born facades without folklore
deferred entry, derived, and worthy-derived follow-on surfaces are named and routed without placeholder crate births
Milestone 1 closes with routing proof rather than empty boxes or smuggled later-class behavior
phases.instructions: Implement Phase 7 as the narrow public proof closeout. Route the exemplar family across the born classes and the deferred naming surfaces without birthing speculative crates.
phases.qa_focus: No placeholder births, no deferred class smuggling, and no exemplar that exists only as prose.
